metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Only for accepted issues; disallowed for issues marked 'good first issue'; drive-by PRs without an accepted issue are closed.
domains.accountability_holder: The contributor submitting the PR/issue (repeated 'you must' disclosure and verification obligations placed on the submitter).

evidence.quote: All AI usage in any form must be disclosed. You must state the tool(s) you used
Pull requests with AI-generated code can only be for accepted issues.
AI-generated code must have been fully verified with human use.

domains.reasoning: The policy names PRs, issues and comments explicitly, sets disclosure and human-verification supervision, scope limits (accepted issues only, no good-first-issue), and repeatedly places obligations on 'you' (the submitting contributor), which functions as an accountability assignment for the output.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots at all
domains.reasoning: The policy text never discusses recorded meetings, notetaker bots, or closed/small-group discussion capture.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to non-code media/text: art, images, videos, audio, and text other than code.

evidence.quote: No AI-generated media or text (other than code) is allowed (art, images, videos, audio, etc.).

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named for content ban
domains.reasoning: This clause names content-like categories (art, images, video, audio, non-code text) and bans AI generation of them outright, but it does not say who is answerable for a violation or for verifying compliance, so accountability is missing.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of AI use in moderation actions
domains.reasoning: The policy does not discuss AI being used to moderate, ban, warn, or otherwise police community members; it only discusses closing non-compliant PRs, which is an enforcement mechanism applied to AI content, not AI performing moderation.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to posting code reviews on the repository.

evidence.quote: Agents are strictly forbidden from interacting with our repository. This includes but is not limited to posting issues, making pull requests, posting comments, posting code reviews

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named for who must review
domains.reasoning: The policy explicitly bans AI/agents from posting code reviews, but it never designates who (which role, e.g. maintainer or contributor) is accountable for reviews being human-performed beyond the generic requirement that interactions be done by 'a human'.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Any interaction with the repository (issues, PRs, comments, reactions, reviews, etc.) by an autonomous agent.
domains.accountability_holder: The human who would otherwise let an agent act ('Any interaction on our repository must be done by a human.')

evidence.quote: Agents are strictly forbidden from interacting with our repository.
Any interaction on our repository must be done by a human.

domains.reasoning: Autonomous/agentic action is explicitly named and banned outright, with the requirement that a human perform any interaction instead, which assigns accountability to a human actor even though no specific named role is given.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of energy, water, or carbon impact
domains.reasoning: The policy's rationale section discusses reviewer time and 'slop' PRs but never references energy, water, or hardware/carbon footprint concerns, so there is neither a rule nor a lean on environmental impact.

domains.rationale_only_mention: We have experienced an increasing number of low-quality pull requests that consume significant amounts of human reviewers' time... which can have a net-negative effect on the maintenance of Polars.
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on server load or hardware cost strain
domains.reasoning: The rationale cites strain on maintainers' time and project maintenance as the reason for restricting AI-generated code, which is a human-resource concern rather than server/hardware infrastructure, but it does voice a restrictive concern adjacent to burden on the project; no actual rule about infrastructure (servers, hardware financing) is set.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of training data use or platform user data
domains.reasoning: The policy never discusses how AI models are trained, whether contributor or user data may be used for training, or any related consent question.

unscoped_statements.quote: Issues and discussions can use AI assistance but must have a full human-in-the-loop.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: Polars' AI policy is highly specific and restrictive about code contributions (issues/PRs/comments) and about autonomous agent interaction and AI-driven review, requiring disclosure and human-in-the-loop verification and banning agents from directly acting on the repo; it partially bans AI-generated non-code content but never names an accountability holder there or for review, and it is entirely silent on notetaker bots, moderation, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and training data.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
